requirements.evidence: app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:25-32 locks the queue row and rejects inactive queues from fresh DB state; :71-74 limits candidates to waiting tickets of the given queue; :90-96 orders priority desc, issued_at asc, id asc; :81-87 implements any/priority_only/normal_only; :102-115 checks the last 3 calls (called_at desc, id desc) for the fairness rule; :45-61 locks the candidate, re-checks it is waiting, skips called ones, sets status/called_at/called_by_user_id and returns the updated model. app/Enums/CallMode.php:5-7 and app/Exceptions/NoWaitingTicketsException.php:7 match the contract, including defaulting to CallMode::Any (:20) and reusing InactiveQueueException.

conventions.evidence: The domain write lives in app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:15 (Actions pattern), ships with Pest tests (tests/Feature/CallNextTicketTest.php:14) and updates both required docs (docs/architecture.md:129-147, docs/business-rules.md:121-137). Deviations: the CHANGELOG entry is duplicated under the already-released [0.0.0] section (CHANGELOG.md:39) and the public __invoke has no PHPDoc (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:20) although the private helpers do.

security.evidence: No authorization is required by the task and the action documents that the caller authorizes (docs/architecture.md:145). No request input, Blade output or Livewire is added; the action assigns only the three allowed fields directly rather than through mass assignment (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:56-59) and re-reads the queue under lock instead of trusting the passed model (:25-30). No secrets or unsafe output paths.

tests.evidence: Pest tests cover ordering/tie-break (tests/Feature/CallNextTicketTest.php:46-56), the returned and persisted model (:58-70), queue isolation and never re-calling (:72-82), empty/ineligible modes (:84-93), inactive queues (:95-103), mode filtering (:105-115), the fairness trigger (:117-129, :141-154), called_at tie-break (:174-184) and the concurrent-skip path (:186-200). Gaps: the 'reset' case leaves only two priority tickets after the normal (:125-128), and write-once (only status/called_at/called_by_user_id change) is never asserted.

simplicity.evidence: One focused action with a FAIRNESS_WINDOW constant (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:18), reusing the existing Ticket/Queue models, TicketStatus and InactiveQueueException; no new layers or speculative abstractions. Minor: the any-mode branch builds the full-ordering query twice through the ?? fallback (:84-86), and mustCallNormal is recomputed on every skip iteration (:65).

readability.evidence: Small focused methods (pickCandidate :69-88, byFullOrdering :90-96, mustCallNormal :102-115), clear names, and comments explaining the locking/skip rationale (:23-24, :34-35, :98-101); style matches a sibling action.

scope.evidence: Everything in the diff serves the task: the action, enum, exception, docs and tests are all requested. The only unrelated edit is the duplicate CHANGELOG line added under the released [0.0.0] section (CHANGELOG.md:39).

issues.explanation: The new CallNextTicket entry is also added under the already-released [0.0.0] - 2026-07-07 section, which misstates when the feature shipped; it belongs only under [Unreleased] (CHANGELOG.md:12).

The fairness-reset assertion does not actually exercise 'three more priority calls allowed': after the forced normal only two priority tickets remain, so the final normal2 assertion would pass even if the reset were broken.

The concurrency test simulates the race with a global Ticket::retrieved listener and a query-builder update instead of Ticket::call(), and never flushes the listener, so it leaks model event state into later tests.
No test asserts the write-once rule that only status, called_at and called_by_user_id change, even though task requirement 8 calls it out explicitly.
The public __invoke has no PHPDoc while conventions ask for PHPDoc on touched public methods; the private helpers have it.
The any-mode branch repeats the full-ordering selection through the ?? fallback; a single named 'pick full ordering' call would read slightly cleaner.

review.summary: Implements App\Actions\CallNextTicket with CallMode and NoWaitingTicketsException, transactional queue/candidate locking, deterministic priority/age/id ordering and the 3-call fairness rule, plus the required docs and a broad Pest test. The contract and edge cases are met, so the change is approvable; the nits are a duplicated CHANGELOG entry under the released 0.0.0 section and a fairness-reset test that never actually exercises three more priority calls.
